title: Slow Capital
style: adult contemporary, british alt-rock, female vocals, reflective mood, driving midtempo drums, layered electric guitars, warm bassline, clean melodic production
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The LSE was both more and less
Rigorous, heavy, a city stress
London was new in its scale and density
Finding the part that suited me
Halls in the first year, then shared flats
Stockwell to Vauxhall, avoiding the traps
Social inside, though I kept my guard
Building my principles, working hard

[Chorus]
Moving through London, learning the flow
Finding out what I actually know
Easy connections, free and light
Infrastructure in the city light
Not for the trade, but the slow capital
Building the world, practical

[Verse 2]
Boyfriends and hookups in those young years
Provisional stories, no lingering tears
Learning what mattered and what was a waste
Finding my direction, finding my taste
Father talked Midlands at dinner tables
Ports and the bridges, concrete and cables
I saw the expertise behind the cash
Long-cycle planning, avoiding the crash

[Chorus]
Moving through London, learning the flow
Finding out what I actually know
Easy connections, free and light
Infrastructure in the city light
Not for the trade, but the slow capital
Building the world, practical

[Bridge]
Financial advisory, client facing
Cross-cultural fluency, no time chasing
Moving through languages, reading the room
Construction accounts in the economic bloom

[Outro]
Clear-eyed and ready, 2012
A life of my own, taking it myself
London, London, infrastructure lines
Slow-moving capital, design
